title: Finite constant parameter scheme for homomorphisms from torus torsion
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], $n\geq1$ and $r,s\geq0$ integers. Put $H=(\mu_n)^r$ and $T=(\mathbf G_m)^s$ with their product group structures [def-sc-gm-ga, def-sc-group-scheme], including the trivial group for a zero exponent. Put $M=(\mathbf Z/n\mathbf Z)^{\{1,\ldots,s\}\times\{1,\ldots,r\}}$ and let $C=\coprod_{m\in M}\operatorname{Spec}k$ be the finite constant scheme. For every $k$-scheme $X$ [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-scheme-over-base], there is a bijection, natural in $k$-morphisms $X'\to X$, between $k$-morphisms $X\to C$ and $k$-morphisms $\phi:X\times_kH\to T$ which are group homomorphisms in the $H$ variable: for every commutative $k$-algebra $A$ [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient] and $x\in X(A)=\operatorname{Hom}_k(\operatorname{Spec}A,X)$, the map $h\mapsto\phi(x,h)$ is a homomorphism $H(A)\to T(A)$, naturally in $A$. Products are fibre products [def-pc-fibre-product]. On the component labelled by $m=(m_{ji})$, the corresponding family is $\phi(x,(h_i))=(\prod_i h_i^{m_{ji}})_j$; exponents are independent of their lifts to $\mathbf Z$ because $h_i^n=1$.

source.place: Lemma 12.35, printed p.243; its finite split diagonalizable case, with the explicit character labels from Lemma 12.4 and Theorem 12.9(a), printed pp.232--233.

proof.text: Put $N=(\mathbf Z/n\mathbf Z)^r$. Write $A[N]=\bigoplus_{v\in N}Ae^v$, with $e^ve^w=e^{v+w}$. On an affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq X$, the open-fibre-product lemma identifies $U\times_kH$ with the open subscheme $p^{-1}(U)$ of $X\times_kH$, $p$ the first projection, and the affine fibre-product formula identifies $U\times_kH$ with $\operatorname{Spec}A[N]$. Explicitly, the coordinate algebra of $H$ is the tensor product of $r$ copies of $k[t]/(t^n-1)$; its mutually inverse maps with $k[N]$ send $t_i$ to $e^{\bar e_i}$ and $e^v$ to $\prod_i t_i^{\tilde v_i}$. These are well-defined multiplicative maps since $t_i^n=1$, and are inverse on the generators. Tensoring these maps with $A$ gives the displayed identification: $a\otimes e^v\mapsto ae^v$, with inverse $ae^v\mapsto a\otimes e^v$. The group operations become $\Delta(e^v)=e^v\otimes e^v$ and $\varepsilon(e^v)=1$ by their formulas on each $t_i$. The tensor product $A[N]\otimes_AA[N]$ has basis $e^v\otimes e^w$: the inverse to the coefficient expansion is given by the products of the coordinate projections.

source.place: Proposition 12.3 and Remark 12.6, printed pp.231--232; affine base change by Stacks Tag 01I4 (schemes-lemma-fibre-product-affine-schemes).

proof.text: Let $\phi$ be a family in the statement. On $U\times H$, pull back the $j$-th multiplicative coordinate to a unit $u_j\in A[N]$. The hypothesis gives $\varepsilon(u_j)=1$ and $\Delta(u_j)=u_j\otimes u_j$. These equations follow on universal points, not merely on field-valued points: use the universal $A$-valued point of $U$ and the identity of $H$ for the first equation; for the second use the $A[N\oplus N]$-valued point whose $U$ coordinate is the structure map and whose two $H$ coordinates send $t_i$ to $e^{(\bar e_i,0)}$ and $e^{(0,\bar e_i)}$. The asserted group-homomorphism identity at this commutative $k$-algebra is exactly the second equation.

source.place: Lemma 12.35 and the family condition in Theorem 12.36, printed p.243; coordinate argument extending Lemma 12.4.

proof.text: Write uniquely $u_j=\sum_{v\in N}a_{jv}e^v$. Comparing the coefficients of $e^v\otimes e^w$ in the preceding equation gives $a_{jv}^2=a_{jv}$ and $a_{jv}a_{jw}=0$ for $v\ne w$; the counit equation gives $\sum_va_{jv}=1$. Conversely these three coefficient relations imply both equations by expansion. This uses no domain or reducedness assumption on $A$.

source.place: Lemma 12.4, printed p.232: its comparison of coefficients gives a complete set of orthogonal idempotents; retain the idempotents over the base ring.

proof.text: Regard $m\in M$ as a tuple $(m_1,\ldots,m_s)\in N^s$ of rows, and set $b_m=\prod_{j=1}^sa_{j,m_j}$. These are idempotents, $b_mb_{m'}=0$ if $m\ne m'$, and $\sum_mb_m=\prod_j(\sum_va_{jv})=1$. Also $\sum_{m:m_j=v}b_m=a_{jv}$. By the idempotent--clopen bijection, the opens $U_m=D(b_m)$ form a disjoint clopen partition of $U$. On $U_m$, $b_m=1$, hence $a_{j,m_j}=1$ (multiply $b_m$ by this idempotent), and every other coefficient in row $j$ is zero by orthogonality. Thus $u_j=e^{m_j}$ on $U_m\times H$. Conversely a clopen partition of $U$ gives its indicator idempotents $b_m$ and the coefficients $a_{jv}=\sum_{m:m_j=v}b_m$, recovering the same partition and units.

source.place: Tag 00EE (lemma-disjoint-decomposition), combined with the explicit coefficient comparison of Milne Lemma 12.4.

proof.text: The coproduct-of-copies lemma, with base $\operatorname{Spec}k$ and label set $M$, identifies such partitions with $k$-morphisms $U\to C$. The construction commutes with every homomorphism of $k$-algebras $A\to B$: its coefficients are sent to their images, as are $b_m=\prod_ja_{j,m_j}$, and the clopen loci pull back because $D(b_m)$ pulls back to $D(b_m\text{ in }B)$. In particular the partitions constructed on two affine opens of $X$ agree on their overlap: cover that overlap by affine opens $W$, compare the two coefficient expansions after restriction to $W$, and use their uniqueness. No intersection of affine opens is assumed affine. The pieces therefore define a global $M$-indexed clopen partition $(X_m)$ of $X$, and hence a unique map $f_\phi:X\to C$ by the same coproduct-of-copies lemma.

source.place: Tag 03YW (example-constant-group): locally constant maps as the functor of points of a constant scheme; affine overlap comparison is the explicit coefficient argument above.

proof.text: Conversely let $f:X\to C$ and let $(X_m)$ be its clopen partition. The scheme idempotent--clopen bijection gives indicator sections $c_m\in\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)$. Put $Y=X\times_kH$ and also write $c_m$ for their pullbacks to $Y$. Let $h_i\in\Gamma(Y,\mathcal O_Y)^\times$ be the pullbacks of the coordinate units of $H$. Define $u_j=\sum_mc_m\prod_i h_i^{\tilde m_{ji}}$. Its inverse is $\sum_mc_m\prod_i h_i^{-\tilde m_{ji}}$, since the $c_m$ are orthogonal and sum to $1$. By the affine fibre-product formula, $T=\operatorname{Spec}\bigotimes_{j=1}^sk[t_j,t_j^{-1}]$; by the tensor universal property, sending the $j$-th Laurent coordinate $t_j$ of $T$ to $u_j$ gives a $k$-algebra map to $\Gamma(Y,\mathcal O_Y)$ (send a Laurent monomial to the corresponding product of these units). The natural affine-target adjunction gives a unique $k$-morphism $\phi_f:Y\to T$. On $X_m\times H$ this is precisely the stated monomial formula. The relations $h_i^n=1$ show independence of lifts; multiplication of these monomials shows the group-homomorphism condition after every $k$-algebra base change.

source.place: Tag 01I1 (lemma-morphism-into-affine); indicator sections from Tag 00EE (algebra-lemma-disjoint-decomposition), extended to schemes; monomial labels from Milne Lemma 12.4.

proof.text: These constructions are inverse. Starting from $f$, on each $X_m$ its coordinate expansion has coefficient $1$ exactly in row position $m_j$, so the extracted partition is the original one. Starting from $\phi$, step 4 shows on every affine open that the reconstructed units $\sum_mb_me^{m_j}$ equal $\sum_va_{jv}e^v=u_j$. The opens $U\times_kH=p^{-1}(U)$, $U$ running over the affine opens of $X$, cover $Y$ by the open-fibre-product lemma. The two maps to the affine scheme $T$ therefore have identical coordinate sections on this open cover of $Y$; the structure sheaf makes these equal globally, and the affine-target adjunction makes the morphisms equal. For any $g:X'\to X$, the indicator sections become $g^\sharp(c_m)$ and their loci become $g^{-1}(X_m)$ by the scheme idempotent--clopen lemma. The monomial formula consequently pulls back to the same formula on $X'\times H$. Since the constructions are inverse, this proves naturality of both directions for every $k$-morphism $g$, not only for affine source or target.

source.place: Tag 01I1 (lemma-morphism-into-affine), naturality; Tag 00EE (algebra-lemma-disjoint-decomposition), indicator sections and inverse images.

proof.text: Finally $M$ is finite since $n\geq1$ and both index sets are finite. If $s=0$, then $M$ is a singleton, $T$ is the trivial group, and both sets of maps are singletons; in the construction $b_m$ is the empty product $1$. If $r=0$ or $n=1$, then $N$ and $M$ are singletons; the identity equation forces every $u_j=1$. For $X=\varnothing$ both maps are unique and all partition pieces are empty. Thus the formulas include all stated zero-exponent and empty-scheme cases.

source.place: Lemma 12.35, finite split case; empty-product conventions in the statement.
